body:
I'm looking at this and I have some comments.

1st comment: good job everyone! Makes me happy to see motion blur progressing. it was a long and large team effort and it makes me happy to see everyone working together!

A couple of question
1. Why is it a camera effect and not a world environment effect? Was this dicussed somewhere? what's the rationale?
2. I see that `show in editor` for motion blur is a project setting. I wonder if it should be editor setting. Thoughts? If it's project setting it will be synced across collaborators on a project with git.

Critique:
1. I still feel like the properties about the tile (size and clamping) is not necessary to be exposed to the user. What are the different usecase for those? If they really need to be exposed, they should have more comprehensible names. I still don't understand what they're for.
2. What passivestar said about the property names. camera stuff should have `camera` prefix because right now it's extremely unclear of what is what without reading the tooltip
3. The default camera rotation blur imo should be much lower. I'm part of those people that get motion sick very easily and it's very disorienting as it is now.
4. I don't understand the usecase for fixed framerate. Sounds like something that was exposed "because why not" more than an actual usecase? If that's indeed the case, it should be removed until there's demand. I may 100% be wrong on this, so if there is a usecase please supply it.
5. I am a bit confused about reference framerate at 30, can somebody elaborate on why 30 and not 60?
6. Velocities threshold should be under a toggle instead of changing behaviour when they're both at 0 (unless i misunderstood how they work). It looks like a niche usecase to want to wiggle those manually.

Final thoughts:

I know we've discussed this at length but I still think there should be clearer options for what type of game needs what settings at what value. I understand that racing games, fps games, top down games etc will all have different needs, but as it is right now it's hard to understand the correlation between a property and the kind of game it suits at what value. The naming is a bit aseptic and I think we should sacrifice a bit of precision and technicality in the naming in favor of better clarity for someone that doesn't know in-depth how motion blur works.

Tested locally (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/ef02314f2bd0305035ecbe907883401a393da7a7), it works as expected.

**Testing project:** https://github.com/Calinou/godot-reflection

## Preview

Recorded with Movie Maker mode at 60 FPS:

### No motion blur

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2683c4a-0ae5-497b-9e29-4104f04f90c2

### With motion blur (intensity = 1.0)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64141f04-15b3-4b22-b1eb-aa746b89c387

### With motion blur (intensity = 10.0, time scale = 10.0)

*Very fast motion to see how well it holds up for timelapse-like recordings.*

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a7ab252-ea39-48fc-a2c2-0f03ff8f23de

Some feedback:

- In terms of quality, the effect looks pretty good out of the box. Behavior matches what I expect when the framerate varies; it doesn't get overwhelming at FPS < 30, and reduces itself at higher framerates to avoid the soap opera effect.

- Motion blur is independent of viewport resolution (as expected).

- However, motion blur is affected by `Engine.time_scale`, as `time_step` in RendererSceneRenderRD takes it into account. This also affects auto exposure.

  - This can cause motion blur to become too strong during slow motion, either during development with the Game tab tools, or during gameplay if not compensated for.

  - While it is possible for the user to cancel out the time scale manually by multiplying the motion blur intensity by `Engine.time_scale`, I wonder if these effects should ignore time scale by default. This would be more consistent with other temporal effects in the engine, such as TAA and SDFGI convergence.

    - If we decide to make this change, it should probably also affect auto exposure as well. This can be done in a separate PR, but we may want to land this in the same release that will feature motion blur to minimize visual changes on upgrade.

- There is no way to use this feature with [physical camera units](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/physical_light_and_camera_units.html#setting-up-physical-camera-units), as this is only exposed in CameraAttributesPractical.

  - Physically accurate motion blur could be implemented based on the shutter speed defined in CameraAttributesPhysical, but this could be left for a future PR.

I've confirmed that it works with DoF and Skeleton. Also I've confirmed works in multiple viewports, but I'm not sure how it will work in XR. We'll probably need someone with an XR device to check it out. cc @godotengine/xr @fire @lyuma @SaracenOne @BastiaanOlij
